alerts.title: Abdominal pain — screen as suspected ADR
alerts.message: Guidelines require screening every patient encounter for suspected adverse drug reactions using the Drug Safety Screening checklist, and all suspected ADRs (mild or severe) must be recorded and reported. Patient P004 presents with abdominal pain on TDF/3TC/DTG. TDF can cause gastrointestinal intolerance and renal-related abdominal symptoms. DTG is also associated with gastrointestinal side effects. Evidence against drug attribution: appetite is preserved and no fever is present, suggesting a non-severe presentation. Non-drug causes such as dietary indiscretion, gastritis, or infection should also be considered. The clinician's plan documents the symptom but does not include ADR screening, an aDSM form, or any diagnostic workup.

evidence.recommended_action: Complete the Drug Safety Screening checklist for this encounter. If ADR is suspected, record it in the ART card/register and submit an aDSM form to NDA. Evaluate non-drug causes of abdominal pain as well.
